The Collection

The nine muses

The first pour is Erato, Thalia, and Urania — love, joy, and dreaming, the three most-gifted moods. The full nine complete the set: a muse for every season of a life.

Erato, Thalia, and Urania are shown in the house's signature vessel — cream label, thin gold border, her emblem in gold line art. Every muse, all nine, can also be poured in any of the four designs above. The remaining six arrive with the full collection.

Made To Order

Bespoke Sacred

Some candles are not chosen from a collection — they are commissioned for a moment. Bespoke Sacred pieces are sculpted forms of devotion: prayer hands first among them, poured in your scent, finished in your colour, and inscribed with a name, a date, or a line of scripture.

Prayer Hands The Cross Madonna & Child Guardian Angel Your Commission
  • Baptisms & christenings
  • Confirmations & first communions
  • Weddings & anniversaries
  • Memorials & remembrance
  • Home blessings
  • Recovery & gratitude

How A Commission Works

Poured for one person

  1. Choose the form. Prayer hands, a cross, a Madonna — or describe the piece you are imagining.
  2. Choose the scent. Frankincense & myrrh for the altar, Polyhymnia's sacred blend, or any scent in the house.
  3. Add the words. A name, a date, a verse — inscribed on the base or written on the card that travels with it.
  4. It is poured to order. Sculpted, cured, and finished by hand, then sent to the one it was made for.

Limited Collector Piece

The Guardian

A lion, sculpted smooth in matte ivory and set on travertine — no mane in uproar, no roar. Just watchfulness. The Guardian is the keeper of the house: of thresholds, of altars, of the rooms where the other candles burn.

He is not part of the collection. He is released in small numbered drops, and when a drop closes, he does not return in the same form.

$75 · Planned price · Limited drop · Matte ivory on travertine

The Ritual

How a muse is lit

A candle from this house is never just lit. It is lit for something.

I

Still the room

The bath drawn, the journal open, the workday closed. Lighting marks the threshold between one part of the day and the next.

II

Read her line

Each label carries her sentence — light me when you need to pray. Say it, or simply hold the need in mind.

III

Light, and begin

Strike the match. The flame is the smallest ceremony there is — and for the length of the burn, the moment is kept.
